title: PR Sentinel: adaptive baseline performance gating for token throughput and p95
creator: Marco Chen
description: Build an automated CI 'sentinel' that runs a lightweight performance harness on every PR and compares measured tokens/sec and p95 latency vs an adaptive baseline. The sentinel will decide pass/fail for PR gating and create rich, actionable regression alerts in the console. Goals: detect regressions >=5% for tokens/sec or >=10% increase in p95 with low false positives, keep CI runtime <6 minutes per PR, and provide reproducible baselines for post-merge triage.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'perf-sentinel' executes on PRs and finishes within 6 minutes on default runners
Sentinel computes normalized tokens/sec and p95 corrected for sequence length and batch size
Adaptive baseline uses rolling median + MAD over last 30 validated runs for the target model and instance type
PRs that exceed thresholds (default 5% tokens/sec regression OR 10% p95 increase) fail gating and emit a diagnostic report with diffs and links
Regression alerts create a Linear sub-issue and attach Grafana trace links and the reproducible benchmark artifact
implementation_notes: Prototype harness reuses existing ci-benchmark binary (bench-runner) but adds measurements normalization: tokens/sec per accelerator-second and p95 computed from 99th-window smoothing to avoid outlier noise
Baseline store implemented as a tiny time-series in S3 with metadata tags (model, quantization, hw-type, seq-len-dist).

Adaptive threshold math: baseline = rolling_median(window=30); tolerance = max(absolute_floor, k * MAD) where k=2 for tokens/sec, k=1.5 for p95; floor values tuned to avoid flapping on low-volume models
We include guard rails: skip gating for experimental branches (label: perf-exempt) and for PRs touching only docs or tests

To keep CI time bounded, harness runs 3 short synthetic workloads (short/medium/long) rather than a full sweep; each workload is 60s wall time and uses fixed batch/seq settings chosen from historical distribution
notes: 2026-03-01: Created ticket after spike showed intermittent 7% regressions on HEAD when changing KV cache eviction (linked PR). Decided we need a CI-level guard to stop regressive merges.
2026-03-03: Spike completed by Marco; prototype bench-runner added. Observed noise on p95 when run on shared runners; added median+MAD smoothing to reduce false positives.
2026-03-05: Design review with PM + SRE. Trade-offs: longer CI runs reduce noise but slow dev velocity. Agreed on 3 x 60s workloads and adaptive baseline to balance both.
2026-03-07: Implemented baseline persistence to S3 and lightweight metadata tagging. Chose rolling window=30 after simulating flakiness on window sizes 10/30/90.
2026-03-08: UX review with Console team - decided the sentinel will post a rich verdict comment on PRs with links to failing workload traces and a suggested rollback label.
2026-03-09: Security signoff not required for artifact metadata, but KMS must be used for production baseline storage when we flip to dedicated runners (follow-up: ENG-9522).
2026-03-10: First end-to-end runs on staging CI. Two false positives observed; reduced sensitivity by raising tokens/sec floor and switched to MAD instead of std-dev for robustness.

2026-03-12: Prototype PR opened for internal dogfooding (link above). Next: add automatic rerun job on suspected flaky failures and wire alerting into Console's rollout dashboard. Assigned to Aisha to finalize and harden for rollout to runtime-1.22.

Reviewer feedback (Bethany Li): please add per-model calibration knobs and a way to mute models where hardware variance is inherently high. Action: add labels 'perf-calibrate' and an API to set per-model thresholds.
Follow-up tasks: ENG-9510 (rerun orchestration), ENG-9522 (baseline encryption + dedicated runner storage), PM-441 (pricing/ops review for added CI cost)
If a PR gates fail, the sentinel will automatically create sub-issue(s) under this ticket with the key prefix pattern ENG-9457-*.
next_steps: Finish prototype PR and gather dogfood feedback from runtime team (target 1 week)
Add automatic rerun + flakiness detection to reduce developer friction
Expose per-model threshold overrides in Console and a quick 'rebaseline' workflow for stable commits
Plan rollout: gated on runtime-1.22 canary + 2-week observation window before enforcing hard fails
